title: The Magic Stone That Was Tested on a Prisoner

sections.name: The Magic Stone That Was Tested on a Prisoner
lines: For centuries, rich Europeans paid fortunes for a magic stone. A bezoar.
Bezoars are hard lumps that form in the stomachs of animals like goats. They were believed to cure any poison.
In 1567, the king's surgeon, Ambroise Paré, said he thought it was nonsense. So they tested it.
A cook was due to be executed for stealing. He was offered a deal. Take poison, then the stone. If he lived, he'd go free.
He took the poison, then the bezoar. Hours later, he died.
The bezoar did nothing. It's one of the first recorded experiments testing a medicine.
